reports.title: Trump Threatens More Bombs While Claiming Peace Progress on Iran
reports.subtitle: Sixty-eight days into a US war with Iran, both sides are inching toward a one-page memorandum while the president simultaneously threatens to escalate.

reports.title: Trump's AI Team Is Rebuilding Everything It Burned Down
reports.subtitle: After dismantling Biden's AI safety framework, the White House is now building a near-identical system with a different label and a political score to settle.

reports.title: The $166 Billion Tariff Refund Is Starting to Pay Out
reports.subtitle: After the Supreme Court struck down Trump's Liberation Day tariffs, importers are getting real money back. The mechanics of that repayment expose exactly how much the policy cost.

reports.title: SCOTUS Just Handed Republicans a Redistricting Weapon Before the Midterms
reports.subtitle: The Supreme Court's 6-3 ruling in Louisiana v. Callais dismantled majority-Black congressional districts. States are now scrambling to redraw maps before this year's elections.

reports.title: Every Government Is Banning Children from Social Media. None of Them Know If It Works.
reports.subtitle: The UK has now passed mandatory social media restrictions for under-16s. Canada, California, and Sri Lanka are following. The policy is running ahead of the evidence.

reports.title: SCOTUS Lets Apple's Contempt Finding Stand. Now a Judge Gets to Set the Rules.
reports.subtitle: After five years of litigation, Epic Games wins a procedural victory that sends Apple back to district court to face the one question Apple has been fighting to avoid: how much can it charge?

reports.title: UK Goes to the Polls Today. Labour Is Bracing for Its Worst Night in a Generation.
reports.subtitle: Voting is underway across England, Scotland, and Wales. Reform UK leads national polls at 25%. What today's results mean depends on whether Farage can convert council seats into something durable.

reports.title: Europe Just Blinked on AI Regulation
reports.subtitle: The EU's landmark AI Act has been watered down, delayed, and rebranded as a competitiveness measure. The question is whether that was the plan all along.

reports.title: Trump Goes to Beijing. China Holds the Iran Card.
reports.subtitle: The first US presidential visit to China in eight years arrives after two months of war in Iran, with Beijing in a position it has rarely occupied: indispensable to both sides.

reports.title: Trump Started a War That Is Preventing the Rate Cuts He Wants
reports.subtitle: The Iran war has created an oil-driven inflation shock that is pushing the Federal Reserve toward rate hikes, the opposite of everything Trump has demanded for two years.

reports.title: Trump Wants the Filibuster Dead. His Own Senate Won't Do It.
reports.subtitle: The SAVE America Act is stalled in the Senate not because of Democrats but because Republican senators refuse to eliminate the filibuster to pass it. Trump is furious. Thune is unmoved.

reports.title: Republicans Just Introduced a National Abortion Ban Labeled Something Else
reports.subtitle: Rep. Kat Cammack's Dismemberment Abortion Ban Act criminalizes the most common second-trimester procedure. Call it what it is: a national 12-week ban written to sound procedural.

reports.title: Both Sides Declared a Ceasefire. Both Sides Violated It. Now They're Doing It Again.
reports.subtitle: Russia and Ukraine each announced Victory Day ceasefires, each accused the other of breaking it within hours, and Russia has now announced a second one for May 8-9. This is not a peace process. It is a ritual.

reports.title: China Retroactively Killed a $2 Billion AI Deal. The Founders Can't Leave.
reports.subtitle: Beijing blocked Meta's acquisition of AI startup Manus ten weeks after it was announced, ordered the parties to unwind it, and restricted the Chinese co-founders' ability to travel. The move draws a permanent line: Chinese-origin AI does not get sold to Americans.

reports.title: Trump's Policy of Jailing Immigrants Without Bond Hearings Is Heading to the Supreme Court
reports.subtitle: Federal appeals circuits are splitting over whether a 30-year-old immigration law authorizes mass detention without hearings. The Supreme Court will likely have to decide whether millions of people can be held indefinitely on the government's schedule alone.

reports.title: Trump Just Picked a Surgeon General Who Deleted Tweets Criticizing Him and RFK Jr.
reports.subtitle: The MAHA-MAGA split inside the administration is now visible in public: Trump replaced his MAHA-aligned surgeon general nominee with a Fox News doctor who spent years attacking Kennedy's health agenda, then deleted the evidence.

reports.title: The Jobs Market Looks Fine. The Hiring Market Doesn't.
reports.subtitle: Tomorrow's April payrolls report will likely show near-zero job creation alongside a stable unemployment rate. This is not a healthy labor market. It is a frozen one, and the Iran oil shock is the reason it cannot thaw.

reports.title: Trump Is Getting the Fed He Wanted. The Question Is What He'll Do With It.
reports.subtitle: Kevin Warsh clears the Senate Banking Committee 13-11 and takes over from Powell on May 15. The Fed he inherits is more divided than it has been in decades, and the economy is the opposite of what Trump promised Warsh would fix.

reports.title: Roberts Says the Supreme Court Is Not Political. He Said It the Day After a Partisan Redistricting Ruling.
reports.subtitle: The Chief Justice went to a judicial conference in Pennsylvania to defend the Court against 'political actor' charges, one day after a 6-3 party-line vote stripped majority-Black districts in Louisiana.

reports.title: The US Just Sanctioned a Nickel Mine in Cuba. China's Battery Supply Chain Is the Real Target.
reports.subtitle: Rubio's State Department hit the Moa nickel-cobalt joint venture between Canada's Sherritt International and Cuba's military. Sherritt's shares collapsed and the company ended its participation. The strategic target is not Cuba. It is China.

reports.title: Samsung's Workers Want 15% of the AI Boom. The Company Says No. An 18-Day Strike Starts May 21.
reports.subtitle: Samsung's semiconductor division just posted a $32.6 billion first-quarter profit. The unions that made those chips want a share. Management says the timing is wrong. The timing is never going to get better.

reports.title: Trump Killed Biden's AI Safety Framework. Then He Built the Same Thing and Called It Something Else.
reports.subtitle: The Center for AI Standards and Innovation just signed testing agreements with Google DeepMind, Microsoft, and xAI. It is functionally identical to the AI Safety Institute that Trump disbanded. The question is why it took a near-miss called Mythos to change his mind.
